facts.raw_span: two weeks of fever
generalized weakness, vague abdominal pain, vomiting, headache, body aches, and moderate nasal bleeding
a 2×1 cm submandibular lymph node
hepatomegaly (7 cm below the costal margin)
urea 18.8 mmol/L
creatinine 141 µmol/L
ferritin >40 000 µg/L
pancytopenia: hemoglobin 6.4 g/dL, WBC 1.7×10^3/µL, ANC 0.9×10^3/µL, platelets 2×10^3/µL
bilateral subdural hemorrhages without midline shift
bilateral pleural effusion, extensive pulmonary consolidation, thrombosis of the celiac artery with splenic infarction, mild hepatomegaly, and massive splenomegaly with infarction
13% abnormal blastoid cells of medium size with fine nuclear chromatin, unevenly distributed coarse basophilic granules, and occasional bilobed nuclei
bone marrow aspirate was hypercellular with 26% immature metachromatic blasts

concepts.why: The patient's bone marrow aspirate showed 26% immature metachromatic blasts and 13% abnormal blastoid cells, which are characteristic of AML.
The patient's elevated ferritin level, pancytopenia, and evidence of hemophagocytosis in the bone marrow are consistent with HLH.
The patient's bilateral subdural hemorrhages and thrombosis of the celiac artery are consistent with DIC.
The patient's fever, generalized weakness, and abdominal pain are consistent with sepsis, although the lack of a clear infectious source makes this diagnosis less certain.

rationales.F07: Elevated ferritin levels are commonly seen in Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis.
rationales.F11: The presence of abnormal blastoid cells is highly suggestive of Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
rationales.F12: The bone marrow aspirate showing immature metachromatic blasts is highly indicative of Acute Myeloid Leukemia.

frontier_selector.rationale: High ferritin level, pancytopenia, and evidence of hemophagocytosis in the bone marrow aspirate support Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis, while the presence of blastoid cells and immature metachromatic blasts also suggest Acute Myeloid Leukemia, but the overall clinical picture and laboratory findings are more consistent with HLH.
